about.title: Desert Hot Springs Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Desert Hot Springs sees its share of collisions along Palm Drive, Dillon Road, Pierson Boulevard, and Hacienda Avenue, with public records showing crashes cluster more often on Monday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. Riverside County reported 70 injury collisions here recently, with 99 people hurt and 4 lives lost — numbers that translate into real medical bills, missed work, and stress for local families. Our team handles personal injury claims and can evaluate what happened and explain your options under California law. Whether you were rear-ended near a busy intersection or sideswiped while commuting through town, our understanding of local roads and insurance tactics can make the process less confusing. There's no cost to get started, and we only get paid if your claim results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but claims against a government agency (like a city road issue) can require notice in as little as six months. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of blame — but you can still recover something even if you're partly at fault. We can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you early in the process.

items.title: Skip the Recorded Statement
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, which can be used to minimize your claim later. Speaking with us first, before giving any statement, helps protect what you say and preserves evidence while it's still fresh.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Desert Hot Springs?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, like a public road agency, might be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth getting a quick evaluation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it matter that my crash happened on Dillon Road or Pierson Boulevard?
items.answer: Local roads like Dillon Road and Pierson Boulevard see a fair amount of traffic in Desert Hot Springs, and public collision records help us understand patterns like time of day or intersection layout. This context can be useful when reconstructing how a crash happened, though every case still depends on its own specific facts.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to find out whether you have a viable claim.
